name: Pound
overview: The biblical term "pound" translates the Hebrew word "maneh" and the Greek word "mina," each representing a significant measure of weight and value. In the Old Testament, such as in 1 Kings 10:17 and Ezra 2:69, a pound of gold or silver was a substantial quantity, roughly equivalent to fourteen ounces. In the New Testament, Luke 19:13 uses the Greek "mina" to describe a pound worth about twelve ounces and valued at approximately one hundred denarii, illustrating its considerable economic weight. These passages demonstrate that a "pound" in Scripture was not merely a unit of measure but also a symbol of considerable worth and responsibility.
